_doc: Asset catalogue for Tools/AssetPipeline/pipeline.py. One entry per game asset. Sizes in metres (the pipeline converts to Unreal centimetres on export), budgets in triangles for LOD0. Skeletal meshes get baked LODs with Unreal screen sizes; static meshes use Nanite instead. See Tools/AssetPipeline/README.md.

assets._note: Turf over the playing area, inlaid lines and run-off (GDD 2, GDD 10). Tuning in config/court_surface.json, colours in palette.json court.Turf/Line/Runoff.
Tempered glass walls with their bolt fixings (blender/build_court_glass.py, config/glass.json). Not Nanite: Nanite does not render translucent materials.

Net cloth (a grid the hit reaction bends through MPC_NetReaction), headband tape, border and side bands, lacing, cable, posts, winch and anchor. Not Nanite: its materials use World Position Offset and it is small. bounds_extension_m keeps it from being culled while it bulges.

net._doc: Build sizes in metres, not regulation values (those come from CourtSpec.h). Tape 50-63 mm per the rules; cable at most 10 mm.

assets._note: Steel structure: posts, corner L-posts, mesh panel frames, base plates, gussets, anchors and bolts. Layout in asset_lib/court_frame_layout.py, sections in config/court_frame.json.
One quad per mesh opening; the WireMesh material draws the wires. Not Nanite: it is masked and only a few dozen triangles, so a plain static mesh is cheaper.

The match ball (GDD 2, GDD 10): felt sphere plus a fuzz shell at LOD0, plain spheres at LOD1 and LOD2 (the broadcast camera sees about ten pixels of it). Seam, felt, printed mark and LOD sizes in config/ball.json, colours in palette.json 'ball'. Not Nanite: it is tiny, moves every frame, and the fuzz shell is masked.
The ball's speed trail: a tapered tube 1 m long along -X, stretched and aimed by APadelBall. Translucent, so not Nanite.

The match racket, the invented Ostrel Keystone (GDD 2: 455 x 260 x 38 mm at most, solid, perforated face; GDD 10): diamond head, carbon face with a raised sand finish, 43 drilled holes, open heart with a bridge, alloy weight cartridge and shoulder ports, rubber bumper, overgrip. Layout and graphic in config/racket.json, colours in palette.json 'racket'. Hand-built LODs, not Nanite: it is small, moves with the hand every frame, and the broadcast camera sees it a few dozen pixels long. See docs/decisions/0008-racket.md.

The players' padel shoe with a low white sock (decision 0006): UE 5.8's MetaHuman wardrobe has no footwear, so UPadelPlayerAnimComponent attaches this to each MetaHuman's feet. One mesh for both feet.

vars.object: a courtside bench with a powder-coated aluminium frame and wooden slats
vars.materials: matte dark grey aluminium, oiled oak

assets._note: Indoor hall after docs/art/ARENA_SPEC.md 2: 50 x 46 m, 15 m eaves, roof trusses from 12 m, dark acoustic walls and polished concrete. A stand-in until the arena's parametric builder lands.
The indoor light rig (ARENA_SPEC 6.1): box truss at the court fixture rows of Data/Lighting.json, underside on the 8 m ceiling plane, cross truss over the net, hoists, and the house-light bars.
Outdoor masts, one behind each floodlight in Data/Lighting.json.
Outdoor club ground: concrete pad, lawn, hedges.
Ten-row grandstands on both long sides (ARENA_SPEC 5.1), three aisles, dark slate seats.
Perimeter boards round the run-off, club colours only (no sponsors, no text).
One LED floodlight, lens at the origin facing +X; APadelVenueLighting places one on every fixture.
